title: The Benefits of Knowledge Organisers
author: Dominic Salles
summary: Dominic Salles argues that the number of facts on a knowledge organiser should be deliberately limited, because every fact must be retrieved repeatedly across years. Using spaced-retrieval intervals of roughly one day through six months, he works through the arithmetic of retrieval across Years 7 to 9. A 30-fact organiser demands about 420 quiz questions per organiser over its lifetime, whereas a 50-fact organiser demands about 700, and the numbers compound across six organisers a year. Against 39 homework slots and 121 Do Nows, he shows that 30-fact organisers fit comfortably while 50 facts push Year 9 to 15 questions per Do Now. He notes that most organisers he sees hold 80 to 100 facts, which is too many unless retrieval is fast-paced and spoken, and suggests using ChatGPT to generate multiple-choice, true-false and cloze questions. The post is a planning argument connecting curriculum content selection to retrieval practice workload.
points: A knowledge organiser should contain only what students will still be asked to retrieve in Years 10 and 11.
Spaced retrieval multiplies workload: 30 facts yields about 420 questions over the organiser's life while 50 facts yields about 700.
By Year 9 a 50-fact curriculum requires 15 questions per Do Now once homework quizzes are counted, which is unsustainable.
Organisers of 80 to 100 facts only work if retrieval is quick and spoken rather than slow and written.
Pasting an organiser into an AI tool section by section can generate multiple-choice, true/false and cloze questions to cover the volume.
quotes: So, nothing should really be on a year 7 knowledge organiser which you don’t need students to be asked to retrieve in year 10 and 11. So, If a knowledge organiser has 30 pieces of knowledge, rather than 50, the difference is exponential.

First year 7 knowledge organiser: 30 facts, x 6 retrievals, x 2 retrievals in each of the 4 subsequent years = 420 quiz questions. However, if we include something like plot points, our knowledge organiser now becomes say 50 facts. The same pattern of retrieval now gives us 700 quiz questions.
1170 are covered by homework, leaving 1830 quiz questions to be done in 121 lessons. Now we need 15 questions per Do Now.

Most knowledge organisers I see in schools, in a range of subjects, contain 80 to 100 facts. This is going to prove too many to retrieve properly to lead to long term memory. The numbers will just be too great.

Unless much of the retrieval is fast paced and spoken, without students having to retrieve slowly by writing. How will you generate enough questions? Paste your knowledge organiser into ChatGPT a section at a time.

Research on spaced practice and retrieval suggests that optimum gaps in retrievals are approximately 1 day, 1 week, 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 2 months, 4 months – longer doubling is less clear – so let’s assume 6 months. This would suggest at least 6 retrievals during a school year, and then 1 or 2 retrievals in subsequent years.
